A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualGraph study. Their text, rendered figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–I support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations. Appendices E–G contain original cost, KG extraction-reliability and human-evaluation results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original DualGraph benchmark evaluations, ablations and empirical studies in Appendices E–G.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1 and Appendix C retain the same graph updates, search-chain construction, stopping policy and report generation. The appendix syntax and indexing fixes clarify the existing workflow without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DeepResearch Bench, DeepResearch Bench II, DeepResearchGym and DeepConsult. The additional test scenarios and case study in the appendices are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and 5 and Figure 3. All five ablation comparators, including the LightRAG construction variant, already appear in v2.

E3.justification: Judge models, metrics, backbones, the five-round limit, shared initialization, disabled stopping in fine-grained ablations and appendix sample sizes remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The iteration and component ablations, joint-citation evaluation, cost analysis, extraction-error analysis, human validation and case trajectory are retained. Figure 3 redisplays the existing analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds or experimental confidence intervals. Appendix G retains the same human-agreement statistics and calculation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 updates DeepConsult percentages: LangChain-DeepResearch's tie rate changes from 44.60 to 44.61 and loss rate from 40.90 to 40.93; Qwen-Agent's loss rate changes from 91.17 to 91.18. Rankings and DualGraph scores are unchanged. All 60 plotted values in Figure 3 are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11) and Appendix D's search-space bounds, coverage argument and convergence reasoning are unchanged. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: separating knowledge from outline structure and using graph-guided exploration to improve deep research. The four-benchmark claim and headline 53.08 RACE result remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of coverage gains and FACT citation-accuracy differences are retained. Section 5 and the appendices preserve the same limitations concerning computational cost, extraction errors and untested multimodal applicability.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects the w/o-KG UPDATEOG evidence argument from D_t to D_{t+1}, aligning it with the existing update-after-retrieval description. Appendices I.5–I.6 restore missing JSON object braces and clarify ID placeholders. These improve technical documentation without changing extraction or merging rules.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A.4 and the references retain the same cited works and positioning against outline-centric and graph-retrieval systems. Citation phrasing changes do not alter those relationships.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered grammar, citation-phrasing and capitalization edits and updates version/date text. Appendix H corrects duplicated step numbering. The section organization and substantive narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with new colors, larger typography, fewer axis ticks and removal of hatching and numeric bar labels. Figures 4–5 shift slightly, and the corrected prompt examples reflow across pages 28–29. The overall document layout is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes missing JSON structure in Appendices I.5–I.6 and resolves the evidence-index inconsistency in B.3, improving implementation clarity. Figure 3 is less cluttered but loses exact bar labels. The documentation fixes and limited copyediting provide a modest net quality gain while the scientific evidence and conclusions remain essentially unchanged.
